column1: # tools/ci-expected.tsv -- the allow-list `tools/ci-census.py` checks a build against.
# One row per allowed skip. Tab separated:
#   suite   bench_total   allowed_skip_label   covers   reason
# `bench_total` is the number of cases the suite prints WHEN EVERYTHING IT NEEDS
# IS PRESENT -- measured on the bench machine, not read off the source.
# `covers` is how many cases that one skip LINE stands for, and it is
# the field that matters: on a stock runner `tools/test-hazlint.sh` prints eight
# skip lines standing for twenty-five cases, and a census that counted lines
# would have reported eight.
# A suite with nothing to skip gets one row with `-` and 0.
# A suite CI does not run at all is marked `*bench-only*`, and its whole total
# counts as not run. It is listed rather than omitted because a suite nobody
# lists is a suite nobody misses.
# 2026-08-27: test-hazlint 56 -> 96 and test-rlxprobe 195 -> 202, both from the
# COP3 correction in hazlint 1.2. Note what did NOT move: no violation count on
# any artefact in this tree changed, on either tool, before or after. The whole
# of the delta is controls and mutations -- which is the only way a fix that
# moves no number can be shown to have been a fix at all.
# 2026-08-26: spec-check went 10 -> 11 when it gained C8 and a ninth mutation.
# Caught by running ci-census against a fresh spec-check.out BEFORE the push --
# the second time a number in this repository would have been contradicted by
# the very next build (the first was ci.yml's own header, 2026-08-25).
# 2026-08-27 (second session): binsim arrives with two rows. `binsim` is the
# tool's own --self-test, twenty-three controls, none of which needs a vendor binary
# -- deliberately, because hazlint is *bench-only* for exactly the opposite
# reason and that means CI runs zero hazlint cases. `test-binsim` is 71 on the
# bench and 63 on a runner; the eight that stand down are the ones that read the
# six vendor trees. That eight was SEVEN when this row was first written, and
# the arithmetic here is what said so -- 48 + 7 = 55 against a bench total of 56,
# one short, because the section it stands for had eight cases and not seven.
# The suite was 56 then and is 65 now: `--fingerprint` turned out to have no case
# at all (seven added), and E0 -- the corpus's one-ISA membership rule -- got two
# more when a 2025 MediaTek image raised the question of a seventh tree; then 65 ->
# 71 when an adversarial review found three surviving mutants and a manifest no
# runner could reach.
# suite
spec-check
binsim
test-binsim
column5: needs $FWRE_WORK/extracted -- six vendor firmware trees, one of which is this unit's own flash dump, so they can never be committed. Unlike test-hazlint this suite does NOT fail without them: binsim's twenty-three controls and the whole corpus path (manifest, matrices, void verdict, BASE/FLOOR) run against synthetic ELFs built by the suite, so a runner exercises everything except the eight assertions about the real six. 量 2026-08-27 with $FWRE_WORK pointed at an empty directory: 63 ok / 0 FAIL / 1 skip line covering 8, which closes against 71

column1: test-hazlint
column5: its K4 population control is $FWRE_WORK/stage2.bin -- 56 KiB of this unit's own vendor bootloader, which is someone else's property and identifies one physical device. On a runner the suite does not skip everything, it FAILS: 量 2026-08-27, 45 ok / 30 FAIL / 8 skip lines covering 21 cases, which closes against 96. The 14 that stood here was stale and by how much was never checked -- HEAD's own pair measured 26 the same day, and one of those 26 was a defect in this suite rather than in hazlint (see the rc=$? note at the exit-code contract). 56 -> 96 on 2026-08-27: P3, E3, M10-M14 and the K9/K6d controls behind them; M13 and M14 came out of the adversarial review of the first draft, which is also why this row was written three times in one afternoon
